targets.authors: Lutchmaya, S, Baron-Cohen, S, Raggatt, P, Knickmeyer, RC, Manning, JT.
targets.title: 2nd to 4th digit ratios, fetal testosterone and estradiol
targets.evidence_quote: Lutchmaya et al. (2004) reported that the ratio of testosterone (T) to estradiol (E) present in second-trimester amniotic fluid was negatively correlated with digit ratios for the right hand (but not the left hand) in a sample of 29 children at 2-year follow-up. This observation is frequently cited as evidence for the measure’s validity but has not been replicated. We therefore present the findings of another study of amniotic T and E that did not find evidence for these effects at 4½-year follow-up.
targets.outcome_quote: We therefore present the findings of another study of amniotic T and E that did not find evidence for these effects at 4½-year follow-up. The confidence intervals were large, the direction of correlations observed was generally erratic, and the overall findings question the premise that second-trimester sex hormones affect the development of digit length ratios in humans.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Abstract states that another sample did not provide evidence for the original effects, and the overall findings question the premise. Large confidence intervals alone do not establish an uninformative author verdict.
